clue.text: Look long and steadily around the Spanish lake for graceful ruminant

indicators.note: one word goes around the others, enclosing them in its middle

blocks.note: to gaze is to look long and steadily
el is Spanish for 'the'
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone stares at length around a Spanish lake looking for a graceful grazing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish article and the lake abbreviation sit together inside the four-letter word for staring.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a slender, graceful antelope, and antelopes chew the cud, so it is a ruminant.

clue.text: EU regulated typical producers of oil

indicators.note: regulated suggests things set in a new order, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that Brussels bureaucracy regulates even ordinary oil producers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'EU regulated' as Brussels rules; in fact EU stays put and 'regulated' works on the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees, plural eucalypti, yield eucalyptus oil from their leaves, so they are oil producers.

clue.text: Flowering shrub in Buck's fizz in Las Vegas

blocks.note: first meaning: an acacia-like plant with fluffy yellow flowers
second meaning: the American name for orange juice mixed with champagne

explanation.walkthrough: Buck's fizz is the British name for champagne with orange juice; in America the same drink has another name, which is also the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a yellow-flowered acacia shrub and, in the US, a cocktail of sparkling wine and orange juice.

clue.text: Intensity of pressure between river and loch

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
P is the symbol for pressure
Loch Ness, the Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A description of pressure building between a river and a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' just places the pressure piece in the middle, so the pieces read river, pressure, loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepness of a colour or feeling is its depth, its strength or intensity.

clue.text: Duplicate flags showing inconsistent values

blocks.note: a duplicate is a double
standards are flags or banners

explanation.surface: Two identical flags flown side by side reveal a contradiction in principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Double standards are moral rules applied differently to different people, an inconsistency of principle.

clue.text: Wrap up hours dithering in goal

indicators.note: something dithering cannot settle, so the letters of the word before it wander into a new order
one piece sits inside another, here placed within the word that follows

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes hours to wrap things up while hesitating over their objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' suggests finishing a task; here it means literally to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshroud is to cover or wrap something completely, as in a burial cloth.

clue.text: Bottle stocked by Pilsner vendors

indicators.note: the letters are held in stock within the following words, carried by them

blocks.note: the run of letters across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A bottle of beer on sale from people who sell Pilsner lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container for the Pilsner, but it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and nerve is the same steady boldness.

clue.text: Drink stirred more for big shot

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cocktail stirred with extra ingredients, made for an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink stirred' reads like a cocktail instruction; 'Drink' is the verb and 'stirred' acts only on the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, an informal term like big shot for someone powerful.

clue.text: Dog's a little monkey consuming peeled plum

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outer letters of the fruit word are stripped away
one word eats the other, taking it into its middle

blocks.note: the saki is a small South American monkey
the fruit word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A dog behaves like a little monkey by eating a peeled plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's a little monkey' reads as a remark about a cheeky pet; the apostrophe-s is just 'is' linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender, fast hunting breed, a type of sighthound from the Middle East.

clue.text: Removes ties from box sent west on Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means right to left, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Unst is the northernmost of the Shetland Islands
to box is to spar

explanation.surface: Someone untying a parcel that has been posted westward to a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the island first, with the reversed boxing word after it; Unst is in Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstrap something is to undo the straps, the ties or bands, holding it.

clue.text: Sacrifice in gutless huge combat running amok

indicators.note: without guts means the insides are removed, leaving only the outside letters
running wild out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowardly soldier is sacrificed in a huge battle that has got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutless' looks like a jibe at a coward; here it empties the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was an ancient Greek sacrifice of many cattle, later any great slaughter.

clue.text: Midshipman free to move on after getting rejected

indicators.note: letters set moving shift position into a new arrangement
something rejected is sent back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A young naval officer is free to move on after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' means the turned-round 'on' piece comes after the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer was old naval slang for a midshipman, the junior officer who helped reef the sails.

clue.text: What to do with chess game and how to finish it for companion

blocks.clueFragment: What to do with chess game
blocks.note: you play a game of chess
checkmate ends a chess game

explanation.surface: Advice on playing a game of chess and ending it, offered to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a friend one plays with, a companion in games.

clue.text: Ship's doctor swallowing tail of toughest fish

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used
one word takes the other inside it, as a mouth takes food

blocks.note: a ship's surgeon is its medical officer
the final letter

explanation.surface: A ship's medic gulps down the tail of a very tough fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large, bony-plated fish whose eggs are sold as caviar.

clue.text: Possibly no regret housing a dynamo

indicators.note: a house holds something, so the letter goes inside the preceding words
possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters that follow

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with no regrets about keeping a spare power unit at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' sits at the front and governs both 'no regret' and the added letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine converting motion into electric current, a type of electrical generator.

clue.text: Scotsman supporting whisky dispenser? He can provide glasses

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporter stands underneath, so the Scotsman's name is placed below the dispenser

blocks.note: an optic is a measuring device fitted to an upturned bottle in a pub
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scottish barman stands by the whisky bottle; he can supply glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the name beneath the dispenser. Glasses suggests tumblers for the whisky, but they are spectacles; an optic is the British pub measure on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and dispenses spectacles, the glasses worn to correct vision.

clue.text: Sepal tip dismantled, seed stripped of membrane and halved

definitions.text: seed stripped of membrane and halved

indicators.note: taking something apart lets its letters be put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A botanist takes apart the tip of a sepal and prepares a seed by removing its coat and cutting it in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas with the skin removed and the seed separated into its two halves.

clue.text: Piano song allowed in short dramatic performance

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a song or ballad
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A piano number is permitted in a brief stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlet is a little play, a brief piece of drama.

clue.text: Gradual absorption of brine essentially in enormous northern bog

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so only the central letter of the word is taken
one piece is placed inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
in northern England and Scotland a moss is a peat bog
the central letter

explanation.surface: Salt water slowly soaking into a vast bog in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize; moss as a word for bog survives in northern place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the slow passage of liquid through a membrane, and figuratively any gradual absorption of ideas.

clue.text: Rhubarb has, for the French, no taste perhaps

blocks.note: non is French for no
taste is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A dismissive French verdict that rhubarb has no flavour at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' looks like the vegetable being tasted; in British slang it means nonsense, and 'perhaps' marks taste as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for foolish talk, the meaningless chatter actors mutter in crowd scenes.

clue.text: Revolutionary native of Apollo's legendary birthplace is arrested

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word is flipped end to end

blocks.note: Apollo was said to be born on the Greek island of Delos, whose people are Delians

explanation.surface: A rebel from the Greek island where Apollo was born has been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as an insurgent being arrested; it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed is informal for caught or arrested, as when police finally nail a suspect.

clue.text: Mostly was a big favourite accompaniment for raw fish

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written; that the answer also lies within these words is a coincidence of the trimming, not a hiding device

explanation.surface: Something was nearly always a great favourite served with sashimi.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words are run together and lose their final letter; 'big' might seem to belong with 'favourite' but it is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green Japanese horseradish paste served with sushi and sashimi.

clue.text: American model upset fabulist

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: An American fashion model is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the moral animal fables, so he is the archetypal fabulist.

clue.text: Cartoon technician rejigged main timetable the wrong way

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a rota is a timetable of duties

explanation.definitionFit: An animator draws or models the frames that make cartoons move, a technician of film animation.

clue.text: More specious marginal explanation that is right

blocks.note: a gloss is an explanatory note in a margin
i.e., id est, means 'that is'
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A note in the margin argues that a more plausible-seeming account is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy can mean having a superficially attractive surface, so glossier means more speciously appealing.

clue.text: Part of norteño sisterliness is union

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, the letters sitting within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words, reading the ñ as n

explanation.surface: Northern Mexican sisterhood is held up as a kind of unity.
explanation.walkthrough: Norteño is Spanish for a northerner. Enosis was the movement for the union of Cyprus with Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Enosis is Greek for union, used for the campaign to unite Cyprus politically with Greece.

clue.text: Small gratuity concludes periodical allowances

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tip is a gratuity
ends means concludes

explanation.surface: A modest tip brings a run of regular payments to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipends are fixed regular payments, salaries or grants paid at set intervals.
